summary: The note examines the growing threat to student data privacy as schools adopt digital technologies, citing studies and experts on rising cyber-attacks, legal gaps, technology tools, human error, governance, parent engagement, and EdTech vendor scrutiny. It argues that protecting student data requires a multifaceted approach combining technology, regulatory compliance, governance, training, and a culture of data privacy.
one_line: Overview of rising cyber threats to student data and the multifaceted approach of technology, law, governance, training and culture needed to protect it.
key_facts: A Global Education Privacy Initiative (GEPI) study released September 5, 2023 reported a 120% increase in cyber-attack incidents on educational bodies since 2021.
Educational institutions store sensitive data such as academic records, personal identification data and sometimes health information, which can enable identity theft and financial fraud.
Dr. Samantha Clarkson, in her October 3, 2023 publication, said the legislative framework surrounding data privacy in schools is still catching up with technological advancements.
FERPA in the United States has been in place for decades but often falls short on the complexities of digital data storage and transmission.
The GDPR applies to entities handling the data of EU citizens and offers stricter, more comprehensive data protection; institutions worldwide look to it for guidance.
CyberSecure Solutions introduced a suite of security tools for educational institutions on September 15, 2023; CEO Jonathan Hughes said human error is often the weakest link.
A University of Cyber Studies study published December 1, 2023 found 65% of data breaches in educational institutions resulted from phishing attacks or accidental insider disclosure.
As of November 20, 2023, Lisa Franklin's consultancy had guided over 200 US schools in revising their data privacy governance strategies; she urges a privacy-by-design approach.
Franklin recommends comprehensive privacy policies, regular audits, and working with privacy officers.
A Parent-Teacher Cybersecurity Association (PTCA) survey released September 25, 2023 found over 70% of parents are concerned about their child's data privacy but feel inadequately informed.
The PTCA launched a nationwide campaign to foster dialogue between parents, students and institutions on digital privacy.
Emily Torres's October 12, 2023 investigative report found not all EdTech companies meet the highest data privacy standards, prompting calls for stronger vetting and contract stipulations.
